note: The symptom is countable, so the predicate counts rather than guesses. It matches an LLVM metadata *node definition* whose contents are four or more Define entries -- the repro passes exactly two -D flags, so a correct compile emits a two-entry !dx.source.defines node (`!N = !{!"DefineA=1", !"DefineB=0"}`) and this cannot match it, while the duplication the issue reports (`!71 = !{!"DefineA=1", !"DefineB=0", !"DefineA=1", !"DefineB=0"}`) has four and does. `{3,}` rather than `{3}` so a partial or triple duplication is not scored clean. Order-agnostic, so an AABB ordering matches as well as the reporter's ABAB. POSITIVE, deliberately: an absence-shaped predicate (e.g. not_regex on a repeated define) is satisfied for free by any compile that emitted no debug info at all, or failed outright, and would report such a run as fixed -- see expected.md. Anchored to `!\d+ = !\{` so it can only match a metadata node definition; in particular it cannot match !dx.source.args, which also carries the -D tokens but begins `!"-E"`. CONTROLS, all captured: variant-onedefine-* (--expect no-match) passes a single -DDefineA, so its node holds one entry when correct and two when duplicated -- neither is four, and the predicate must stay silent, which is what shows it is counting duplication rather than merely spotting the string `DefineA`; variant-nodefines-* (--expect no-match) passes no -D at all, so the node is empty; variant-minimal-* (--expect match) is a four-line compute shader under byte-identical arguments, an identity control showing the duplication belongs to the driver and not to the reporter's shader. COMPANION: match-defines-present.json is the anchor -- it asks only whether a defines node with any entry was emitted, so a `no-repro` here can be told apart from a compile that never produced debug information.
